title: Bay of Bengal system set to become Cyclone Akvan tonight; Andhra and south Odisha on watch
dek: The IMD expects the deep depression to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by 19 November and head for the Andhra Pradesh coast, the third storm to threaten the east coast in about three weeks. Heavy rain is forecast from Tamil Nadu to Gangetic West Bengal.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A weather system over the south Bay of Bengal strengthened into a deep depression late on Sunday night and is expected to become a cyclonic storm by Monday evening, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, putting the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts on a pre-cyclone watch. Once it reaches cyclone strength, the storm is expected to be named Akvan, the next name on the list used for the region, as reports have said.

In its national bulletin issued at 2.30 am IST on Monday, the IMD said the system was likely to become a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening and a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday, 19 November, with sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, as it moves north-westwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The department has not yet named a landfall point or time. It forecast heavy to very heavy rain over coastal Andhra Pradesh, north Tamil Nadu and Odisha later this week, and heavy rain at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on 19 and 20 November.

## What happened

At 11.30 pm IST on Sunday the system lay near latitude 10.6°N and longitude 86.7°E, about 760 km east-southeast of Chennai, 870 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 980 km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha, the bulletin said. It had moved north-northwestwards at 8 kmph over the previous six hours and was carrying winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph.

The IMD's forecast table shows a steady build-up over four days. Winds are expected to reach 60-70 kmph by 5.30 pm on Monday, when it becomes a cyclonic storm; 90-100 kmph by late Tuesday night, when it is classed as severe; and 120-130 kmph by 11.30 am on Thursday, when the system is forecast to lie near 14.7°N, 83.4°E, off the north Andhra coast. The bulletin says the storm is likely to "intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast" in the two days after Tuesday.

The department issued a "yellow message", the second stage of its four-stage cyclone warning system, for Andhra Pradesh and the adjoining south Odisha coast. The bulletin was addressed to the chief secretaries of eleven states and union territories, including West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, as well as to the National Disaster Management Authority and the National Disaster Response Force.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, then heavy to very heavy rain at a few places on 19 and 20 November, with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) over north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
- North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal: heavy rain at isolated places on 17 and 20 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 18 and 19 November.
- Odisha: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from 19 to 21 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: light to moderate rain at many places, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November.
- Rayalaseema, eastern Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand: heavy rain at isolated places between 19 and 21 November.

The IMD expects squally winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts from the evening of 19 November until the morning of 20 November, with "phenomenal" sea conditions there in that window. Along the Odisha coast it forecasts winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph from 19 November. It expects localised flooding of roads, waterlogging in low-lying areas, closure of underpasses in cities, damage to kutcha roads, and damage to horticulture and standing crops in Andhra Pradesh from 18 to 20 November and in Odisha from 18 to 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and shipping

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest Bay of Bengal from 16 to 19 November, the central Bay of Bengal from 16 to 20 November and the northwest Bay of Bengal, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, on 19 and 20 November. The Andaman Sea is off-limits until 17 November. The IMD asked fisheries departments and harbour authorities to alert fishing crews, and advised shipping, port and offshore operators to review their preparedness for possible restrictions from 16 to 20 November.

## Background

Akvan would be the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. The names used in the north Indian Ocean are drawn in sequence from a list contributed by 13 countries in the region; Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh, Murasu by India and Akvan by Iran, according to the published list.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast, which forecasters have not settled. Some reports, citing meteorologists, have suggested the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; others have pointed further south. The IMD has given no landfall forecast.

## What happens next

The IMD said its next national bulletin would be issued at 9 am on Monday. If the system strengthens into a cyclonic storm on Monday evening as forecast, the department is likely to move to a cyclone alert and later a cyclone warning for the coast where landfall is expected, the third and fourth stages of its warning system.

## Key numbers

- 760 km: distance from Chennai at 11.30 pm IST on Sunday
- 870 km: distance from Visakhapatnam
- 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph: forecast peak winds on 19 November
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast in isolated spots of north coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19-20 November
- 16-20 November: period of fishing and shipping advisories in the Bay of Bengal
